title: Spreading a single free homotopy normal form from a local ring
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $P$ a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-pc-derived-category] with finite free terms [def-weil-pbc-free-module], supported in degrees $0$ through $d\in\mathbb N$. Fix $y\in Y$, $i\in\mathbb Z$ and $r\in\mathbb N$. Let $Q=\mathcal O_Y^r[-i]$ be the single cochain complex in degree $i$, and let $s:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to Y$ be the canonical morphism. Suppose the termwise pullbacks [def-pc-derived-pullback] $s^*P$ and $s^*Q$ are homotopy equivalent. Then there is an open neighbourhood $V$ of $y$ such that $P|_V$ and $Q|_V$ are homotopy equivalent. Here a homotopy equivalence consists of chain maps in both directions whose composites are chain homotopic to the respective identities. No residue cohomology hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proof, first two paragraphs: local unit-entry cancellation and extension of the finite calculation

proof.text: Lift the prescribed chain maps e.hom and e.inv using lem-pc-finite-free-stalk-chain-map-pair-lift. Obtain V containing y, f and g on the restricted complexes, and eP,eQ identifying their stalk pullbacks with the original stalk complexes, with exact conjugacy equations.

Precompose and postcompose the two homotopies of e by eP.hom/eP.inv and eQ.hom/eQ.inv. The conjugacy equations, functoriality, and cancellation of inverse isomorphisms identify them with homotopies from the pullbacks of f;g and g;f to the pullbacks of the identities.
Apply lem-pc-finite-free-stalk-homotopy-pair-shrink to the fixed endomorphism pairs (f;g,id) and (g;f,id). Obtain W≤V containing y and homotopies between their restrictions.

Use the restrictions of f and g and the two homotopies to construct HomotopyEquiv on the twice restricted complexes. The natural isomorphism restrictFunctorCongr(homOfLE_ι).symm followed by restrictFunctorComp, mapped to complexes, identifies restriction first to V and then to W with direct restriction to W. Transport this homotopy equivalence across those two complex isomorphisms.
